title: Apache ORC (Optimized Row Columnar) format
summary: ORC is a columnar storage format for Hadoop/Spark. File structure: stripes (row groups), each with index, data, and footer; file footer (schema, statistics, stripe locations); postscript (compression codec, footer length, magic 'ORC'). Magic: 'ORC' (0x4F 0x52 0x43) at the end of the file.

ext.summary: ORC is a columnar storage format for Hadoop/Spark. File structure: stripes (row groups), each with index, data, and footer; file footer (schema, statistics, stripe locations); postscript (compression codec, footer length, magic 'ORC'). Magic: 'ORC' (0x4F 0x52 0x43) at the end of the file.

structure.meaning: Index stream (row group offsets) + data stream (column data) + footer (column statistics).
Header (1 byte, version), content length, stripe statistics, row index strides, schema (ProtoBuf serialized), and column statistics.
Compression codec (0 none, 1 zlib, 2 snappy, 3 lzo, 4 lz4, 5 zstd), footer length (variable-length), magic 'ORC' (3 bytes).
'ORC' (0x4F 0x52 0x43) at the very end of the file.

ext.example_decoded: ORC magic at end of file
notes: ORC supports predicate pushdown (skip stripes based on min/max statistics).
Compression: zlib, snappy, lzo, lz4, zstd (per stripe).
ORC is the default format for Hive and is supported by Spark, Presto, and Trino.
ORC includes built-in indexes (row group statistics, bloom filters).
